packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:149 quality-boundary: evidenceForRun accepts any signature-valid finding as a terminal lane without requiring readManifest/readLog, and its coverageDigest only folds manifests/readLogs from passes (lines 154-163). A reviewer can therefore submit a finding with no bounded read evidence, satisfy required-lane completion, and let the critic/finalizer mint a saturation receipt although CHK-003 requires complete mechanical coverage or bounded read evidence for every lane. Require and authenticate read evidence for finding terminals, include it in coverageDigest, and reject lanes lacking it.

packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:138 quality-boundary: findingFamily declares a verified family solely by hashing normalized desc plus severity, while evaluateReviewInventoryWave immediately treats those hashes as verified/new families (lines 207-223). There is no signed independent duplicate/finding-family disposition contract: identical text is silently deduplicated without independent verification, semantically identical findings with different wording are counted as new, and suspected/disproven findings are also labeled verified. This does not deliver CHK-003 E2/A2 or the document promise that raw findings and duplicate claims are independently verified. Add a canonical signed family/disposition artifact consumed by evaluation/finalization; unresolved raw/duplicate claims must remain blockers rather than alter verified-family counts.

packages/main/src/handlers/review-inventory.ts:227 lifecycle-integrity: review_inventory_begin only checks for an OPEN epoch, so it permits a new OPEN epoch while the previous FINALIZED receipt is still unconsumed. packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:284 then independently selects the older FINALIZED/unconsumed pair and authorizes REVIEW->DEV even though the newer OPEN barrier exists. The transition can therefore consume the old receipt, enter DEV, and leave an OPEN epoch that blocks every remediation material write. Reject begin while an unconsumed FINALIZED receipt exists (or make the remediation gate require the authoritative latest epoch and no OPEN epoch), and cover this sequence with an integration test.

doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/review-inventory-epoch-and-saturation-gate.md:85-98 promises every wave folds complete coverage/read evidence into the lane digest before saturation, but packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:149-180 accepts a finding-only lane as terminal even when the finding has no readManifest/readLog and computes coverageDigest from ReviewPass evidence only. packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:537-542 explicitly permits reviewer findings without read evidence. zero-new-saturation-status-bypass: on the RI-003 frozen cutoff, the signed critic receipt leaves the live projection at New verified findings: 4 while renderReviewInventoryStatus reports Blockers: none and Next: lattice review_inventory_finalize. evaluateReviewInventoryWave correctly exposes live.newFamilies, and buildWave would mark this wave saturated=false, but handlers/review-inventory.ts never adds a blocker for live.newFamilies.length > 0 and its critic-complete branch unconditionally selects finalize. Thus DEV-to-REVIEW can proceed with AR_REPORT_MISSING, stale/tampered evidence, or degraded quorum even though the decision document calls the rollout report mandatory. packages/main/src/handlers/review-inventory.ts:415-452 and packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:479-658 — critical concurrency/replay: review_inventory_finalize snapshots the current lane terminals/finding families and writes a FINALIZED receipt, but reviewer finding_add/review_pass_set remain writable while the Story is still REVIEW after finalization. Those evidence writers use separate findings/pass locks, and currentOpenReviewInventory is null once FINALIZED, so a verified finding can be appended immediately after finalization (or race immediately after the inventory lock releases). packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:330-399 then validates/consumes only the frozen epoch+receipt bindings and current material cutoff; it never recomputes the live terminal/finding-set digest. The still-valid old receipt can therefore authorize REVIEW-to-DEV while its immutable aggregate omits the late verified finding, violating inventory completeness and terminal replay safety. Seal terminal evidence at FINALIZED under a shared lock, or make every evidence writer reject/invalidate a pending FINALIZED receipt and revalidate the live aggregate at consumption.

packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:356-362, packages/main/src/handlers/review-inventory.ts:251-255 and 493-496 — FINALIZED receipt recovery is a dead end. The shared writer guard correctly rejects late finding/pass while a finalized receipt is pending and tells the operator to consume or cancel, but review_inventory_cancel only accepts an OPEN epoch and review_inventory_begin rejects the unconsumed FINALIZED receipt. Therefore a legitimately discovered late verified finding cannot be recorded through the supported writer and cannot invalidate or abandon the known-incomplete receipt; the only normal next action is to consume it into DEV. The live aggregate replay cannot detect evidence that the supported writer was forbidden to persist. Add a signed invalidate/cancel/reopen path for an unconsumed FINALIZED receipt (or atomically invalidate and open a fresh epoch when late evidence is attempted), and cover that recovery in the handler smoke test.

F-026 remediation remains bypassable after receipt consumption: assertReviewInventoryEvidenceWritable seals only FINALIZED epochs with !consumedAt (review-inventory-epoch.ts:355-364). consumeReviewInventoryReceipt holds the shared lock only through setting consumedAt and returns (458-492), while REVIEW->DEV publishes story.phase afterward (transition-orchestrator.ts:1443-1448) and does not clear currentReviewRound (the round changes only on entry to REVIEW at 1246-1249). A waiting reviewer finding_add therefore acquires the lock after consumption, passes the now-unsealed predicate, and can append a signed verified finding bound to the still-current old ReviewRun; even after phase publication, finding_add is explicitly allowed in DEV (command-policy.ts:397). That finding is absent from the already-consumed immutable aggregate, and the live aggregate verifier cannot run again because receipt replay is rejected. Existing smoke covers pre-consumption sealing and live tamper before consumption, but not the consume-to-phase-write race or post-consumption reviewer finding. Keep the finalized epoch sealed for its reviewRound after consumption (while allowing a genuinely new reviewRound), or publish the phase/round boundary inside the same serialization fence; add real negative coverage for concurrent/post-consumption finding_add.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:232-247 and packages/main/src/handlers/review-inventory.ts:455-489 — critical wave-boundary evidence loss distinct from F-029/F-030. review_inventory_wave_advance serializes and persists a completed wave, but the OPEN epoch remains writable afterward. assertCurrentReviewRunForEvidence deliberately accepts a non-latest current-round fresh ReviewRun (review-run.ts:1215-1222), so a run started before the checkpoint may submit a verified finding after wave_advance releases the lock. The next evaluation sets waveStart to the prior completedAt and filters candidates by run.startedAt >= waveStart; that old run and its late finding are therefore excluded from the new wave, while the already persisted prior wave cannot be amended. A later zero-new wave can finalize and consume a receipt whose immutable family set omits this signed verified finding. The normal REVIEW gate may still surface an open critical finding, but REVIEW-to-remediation-DEV consumes only reviewInventoryRemediationGate and can proceed with the incomplete aggregate (machine.ts:732-750). Seal completed-wave run IDs, classify evidence by evidence.createdAt with explicit cutoff semantics, or reject terminals for runs started before the current wave; add a real wave_advance-then-old-run-finding negative smoke.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:232-247 and 420-452 — the first wave excludes every current-round finding whose ReviewRun started before epoch.begunAt, while the remediation gate validates only the newly finalized receipt and never reconciles it with the Story existing open verified findings. This is occurring on RI-005 now: F-029 (19:15:20Z) and F-030 (19:17:11Z) predate RI-005 begunAt (19:19:45Z). If fresh lanes correctly avoid duplicating those canonical findings and report no distinct new family, the critic sees rawFindingIds=[], finalization can mint an empty findingSetDigest, and REVIEW->DEV can consume it despite both critical findings remaining open. Cancellation/rebegin has the same loss mode. Seed each epoch with all signature-valid current-round/current-cutoff verified findings (including pre-begin evidence), or add a signed carry-forward/disposition contract and make finalize/consume fail closed unless every open verified finding is represented in the aggregate; add a handler test for finding-before-begin and cancel/rebegin without duplicate re-registration.

findings.desc: Temporal boundaries are not total-ordered, so F031/F032 can still be bypassed within one millisecond. review inventory classifies a run as current-wave when run.startedAt >= wave.completedAt/begunAt and seals it only when run.startedAt < boundary; cancel/invalidate uses the same strict-less-than test. Because all timestamps are millisecond ISO strings, a ReviewRun that actually started before wave_advance/cancel/begin but shares the exact timestamp is accepted as fresh evidence for the next wave. The handler smoke acknowledges this gap by busy-waiting until Date.now() is strictly greater than completedAt/updatedAt/finding.createdAt before exercising wave 2 and rebegin. Thus real execution has no mechanical happens-before identity: an old terminal can satisfy a supposedly independent zero-new wave, and a pre-begin finding whose ReviewRun shares begunAt can be omitted from baselineFindingIds. Replace timestamp-only admission with a signed monotonic boundary (sequence/event identity) or otherwise make equality conservatively old, while preserving an unambiguous way for genuinely post-boundary runs to prove freshness; add deterministic equal-timestamp tests without busy-waits.

packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:267-274 — critical same-wave multi-run omission remains after F029-F032 remediation. For each required lane, evaluateReviewInventoryWave sorts current-wave runs newest-first and selects only the first run with any terminal; rawFindings receives findings only from that one selected run. Yet assertCurrentReviewRunForEvidence explicitly permits a material-fresh non-latest run to write finding/pass evidence (review-run.ts:1215-1222). Therefore two concurrent same-lane runs can order as: older run records a verified finding, newer run records a pass; evaluation selects the newer pass and silently omits the older signed open finding from critic dispositions and the receipt. This is distinct from F031 because both runs start after the same wave boundary. The ordinary REVIEW verdict treats the older open finding as stale-run evidence rather than erased, but REVIEW-to-remediation-DEV consumes the inventory receipt without evaluateReviewVerdict (machine.ts:732-750), so an incomplete aggregate can authorize DEV. Aggregate verified findings from every eligible current-wave run while selecting one terminal only for lane coverage, or reject/supersede terminal writes with an explicit safe rule; add a real two-runs-one-lane finding-then-pass negative smoke.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/review-inventory.ts:53-80,266-303 and packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts:417 — critical frozen-scope bypass distinct from F033/F034. review_inventory_begin signs scopeDigest from the current scope contract and checklist and freezes requiredLanes, but every later freshness consumer (status, critic_set, wave_advance, finalize, and receipt consumption through the cutoff helper) recomputes only materialHash/storyFilesHash; none recomputes scopeDigest or active required lanes. Meanwhile scope_contract_acknowledge is explicitly allowed in REVIEW and appends an acknowledged-expansion to scope-contract.json without changing the frozen material cutoff. Therefore an owner can expand/acknowledge scope after RI-006 begins, retain all old lane/critic evidence, and finalize/consume a receipt bound to the obsolete pre-expansion scope and lane selection. This violates the signed epoch promise that scope and required lanes are frozen and that scope expansion invalidates stale review. Recompute the canonical scope digest and active lanes under the inventory lock at every evidence/finalize/consume boundary, fail closed to INVALIDATED or cancel/rebegin on mismatch, and add a real begin -> scope_contract_acknowledge -> status/finalize rejection smoke.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:87-92,359-453 and packages/main/src/core/mkdir-lock.ts:206-217 — critical cross-process review-pass lost-update family. withReviewPassLock and the outer review-inventory mutation lock use withMkdirLock defaults whose live holder is reclaimed solely after DEFAULT_STALE_MS=10000, but recordReviewPass performs expensive snapshot, candidate/read-diagnostic, provenance, persistence verification, process-event, and auto-commit work; real concurrent RI-006 commands exceeded 10s. In this run quality review_pass_set returned `Review pass B-3f3d:RP-020 recorded`, yet the later authoritative store contained RP-020/RP-021 for concept RR-044 and no pass for quality RR-045; review_inventory_critic_set then failed `REVIEW_INVENTORY_LANES_INCOMPLETE: lattice-review-quality`. A waiter can therefore reclaim a still-live lock, read an overlapping snapshot, reuse IDs, overwrite review-passes.json, and make a command report durable success that is subsequently erased. This is distinct from F033-F035: it is lock liveness/lost-update, not inventory timestamp, run selection, or scope drift. Use ownership-token plus live-PID/heartbeat classification or a non-timeout reclaim contract for reviewer metadata locks, keep the full RMW and final durability check under the non-reclaimable critical section, and add a real two-process >10s review_pass_set stress proving unique IDs and both signed passes survive.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/review-inventory.ts:54-80, packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:1898-1937, and packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts:178 — HIGH, distinct checklist-semantic drift left by the F035 remediation. captureReviewInventoryScope signs only scopeContract plus checklist item id/title/files. The supported verification_intent_repair command remains writable in REVIEW and persists reconstructed verificationIntent rows, but it neither takes the review-inventory mutation lock nor changes any field included in scopeDigest. Therefore after review_inventory_begin an operator can run verification_intent_repair, changing the acceptance/review subject seen by the test-coverage lane, while status/critic/wave/finalize recomputation sees identical material, storyFilesHash, scopeDigest, and requiredLanes and can consume pre-repair lane evidence. The decision contract says supported or direct scope drift must invalidate at the next authoritative consumer. Include the complete checklist review-subject projection, at minimum verificationIntent and related requirement-routing fields, in the signed/recomputed scope digest or serialize and explicitly invalidate every REVIEW-phase checklist semantic writer; add begin -> verification_intent_repair -> status/finalize rejection coverage. Existing focused smokes pass but only exercise scope_contract_acknowledge and do not cover this path.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/review-run.ts:145-183,311-313; packages/main/src/handlers/review-inventory.ts:505-541; packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:271-281 — critical ReviewRun/boundary linearization TOCTOU, distinct from F033. review_run_start acquires the shared inventory lock only for context/cutoff validation, releases it at line 148, then does scope/prompt work and allocates/persists the RR under a different review-metadata lock. Concurrent wave_advance/cancel/begin can acquire the inventory lock in that gap and sign maxReviewRunSequence before the in-flight run is published. The in-flight command then allocates a numerically greater RR and persists it after the boundary, so evaluateReviewInventoryWave and assertReviewInventoryEvidenceWritable classify it as post-boundary even though its startedAt/snapshot/context were captured before the boundary. This violates the decision document claim of a linearized durable identity and can let pre-wave review context satisfy a later wave or escape a terminal boundary. The real >10s two-process review-pass stress passes, so F036 lock-reclaim/ID-loss is fixed; this is a separate cross-lock ordering family. Hold the shared inventory mutation lock across ReviewRun ID allocation and durable run publication with a consistent lock order against the review-metadata transaction, or allocate the monotonic sequence from an inventory-locked counter at publication and bind the run to the exact epoch/wave generation; add a deterministic barrier test interleaving precheck -> wave_advance/cancel -> run persist and require the run to remain sealed/old.
